newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GRAF NOT READY TO MAKE ROOM FOR NEW GENERATION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF NOT READY TO MAKE ROOM FOR NEW GENERATION.

text.p: Steffi Graf showed she is not yet ready to move aside for the new generation, qualifying effortlessly for the French Open third round on Wednesday.
The world number two from Germany took less than an hour to beat French teenager Amelie Mauresmo 6-3 6-3 and clinch her second consecutive straight set success in two days.
Despite not being back at her peak, the 27-year-old German, chasing her sixth title in Paris, received a warm welcome from the noisy, youthful crowd.

"Being back in Paris always means having nice time with the people here", said Graf who appeared relaxed and confident for her second match at Roland Garros after being sidelined for three months due to an injured knee.
"You can tell it's a different atmosphere in the courts and it's great that French tennis has days like that", she said. "It's great to have such a tournament to introduce tennis to kids."
Graf's 17-year-old opponent, who won the junior titles here and at Wimbledon last year, saw her brief appearance as a learning experience.

"That's my first time here as a professional and I know that I have a lot to do. I think the most important is to be mentally fit to face the favourites", said Mauresmo, who beat American Jolene Watanabe in the first round on Tuesday.
Graf, who played with a support on her left knee, had a perfect start breaking in the fifth game to lead 3-2 before wrapping up the first set in 24 minutes thanks to her devastating forehand.
"I have been running around easily and I feel very comfortable now", Graf said of her knee.
The German made a winning comeback last weekend in Strasbourg but her familiar superiority seemed to have faded a little.
"She still has a strong forehand and I was surprised by the speed of her shots but she doesn't seem as confident as she was in previous years", Mauresmo said.
The German broke again in the first game of the second set but committed several unforced errors and had to save three break points while leading 4-3.
Mauresmo's lack of big match experience became clear in the last game when she gave Graf two match points before bowing out on a wide backhand.
